title: Mineral separation protocol for accurate and precise rhenium-osmium (Re-Os) geochronology and sulphur isotope composition of individual sulphide species
author: Saintilan, Selby, et al.

steps.title: Cut and clean samples
steps.instruction: Cut all sulphide samples into slabs and thoroughly clean each slab with silicon carbide grit, followed by rinses with Milli‑Q water and ethanol to remove metal traces introduced during hammering or sawing.

steps.title: Crush and sieve to 70‑200 mesh
steps.instruction: Crush the cleaned slabs using a zirconia ceramic dish and puck, then sieve the crushed material through disposable home‑made nylon sieves to obtain a 70–200 mesh size fraction.

steps.title: Wash fractions and dry
steps.instruction: For each 70–200 mesh fraction, wash with Milli‑Q water using a drip bottle to create a turbulent flow that removes particles finer than 74 µm (200 mesh); rinse the washed fraction with ethanol and dry overnight in an oven at 60 °C.

steps.title: Magnetic separation with Frantz
steps.instruction: Place the dried fraction in a Frantz Isodynamic Separator set to a 15° side slope and 10° forward slope. Apply a 1.1 A current to collect the magnetic arsenopyrite (M1.1 fraction). Then treat the resulting non‑magnetic (NM1.1) sub‑fraction with a 1.7 A current to collect pyrite (NM1.7 fraction).

steps.title: Heavy‑liquid purification
steps.instruction: Purify the magnetic and non‑magnetic sulphide separates by heavy‑liquid separation using Sodium Polytungstate (specific gravity 2.82 ± 0.02). Collect the mineral separates on filter paper in a funnel, rinse them with Milli‑Q water pre‑heated to approximately 40 °C at least ten times to remove the heavy liquid, give a final rinse with ethanol, and dry overnight in an oven at 60 °C.

steps.title: Embed and examine mineral separates
steps.instruction: Embed an aliquot of each arsenopyrite and pyrite mineral separate in epoxy, prepare mounts, and examine them by reflected‑light microscopy. If mineral‑separate quality is uncertain, inspect the mounts with a scanning electron microscope in backscattered electron mode (SEM‑BSE) and optionally perform point wavelength‑dispersive spectroscopy (WDS) for S, Fe, Ni, Cu, and As.
